restatements.text: Names the measure the Improving Transparency, Effectiveness, and Efficiency in California Government Act of 2026.

States findings and declarations that Californians face a high cost of living and tax burden, and asserts that a state spending cap must be protected and public programs must undergo transparency and efficiency audits before raising taxes.
States the purpose is to require the State Auditor to conduct upfront and ongoing audits of programs receiving new or higher special taxes, and to prohibit exemptions from the state spending limit.
Adds Article XXIV to the California Constitution.

Requires the State Auditor to prepare a pre-election financial and performance audit for any proposed special tax initiative. Outlines ten specific metrics the audit must address, requires the Auditor to invite input from the Legislative Analyst's Office, and mandates that an executive summary of the audit be printed in the state voter information guide. Requires the Auditor's reasonable costs to be reimbursed from the generated tax revenue if the initiative is approved.

Requires the State Auditor to conduct ongoing financial and performance audits every four years for any program receiving funds from a special tax enacted on or after January 1, 2026. Costs are to be reimbursed from the special tax revenue.

Prohibits any state tax enacted or taking effect on or after January 1, 2026, from being exempted or excluded from the state's Government Spending Limitation (Article XIII B). Forbids the imposition, collection, or enforcement of any new tax that includes such an exemption.

Defines key terms used in the article, including 'Special tax' as a tax that can only be used to fund specific purposes, and applies the article to all statewide initiative measures on or after January 1, 2026.

Declares that if this measure appears on the same ballot as another measure imposing different audit rules on special taxes or containing a tax exempted from the spending limit, the measure receiving the most votes shall prevail entirely.
Provides that if any part of the act is found invalid, the remaining parts shall remain in effect.
States the act takes effect at the earliest possible date allowed by the state constitution and becomes operative immediately upon taking effect.
Requires the act to be liberally construed to achieve its purposes.

Requires the Attorney General to appoint independent counsel to defend the act if both the Governor and Attorney General refuse to do so. Creates a continuous appropriation from the General Fund to cover the costs of retaining the independent counsel.

evidence.quote: No state tax that is enacted or talces effect on or after January 1, 2026 shall be exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
evidence.why: It limits the state's spending authority by forcing all newly enacted taxes to be subject to the constitutional government spending cap.

evidence.quote: the California State Auditor shall commence with the preparation of a pre-election financial and performance audit
evidence.why: It expands the mandates and workload of a state agency by requiring the Auditor to perform evaluations of proposed special tax programs.

evidence.quote: the California State Auditor shall commence with the preparation of a pre-election financial and performance audit
evidence.why: It strengthens public oversight by mandating financial and performance audits of proposed programs before voters decide on a special tax initiative.

evidence.quote: the California State Auditor shall conduct ongoing financial and performance audits of each program that receives moneys from the special tax.
evidence.why: It expands oversight by requiring recurring reviews for programs funded by newly enacted special taxes.

evidence.quote: a continuous appropriation is hereby made from the General Fund to the Controller, without regard to fiscal years, in an amount necessary to cover the costs of retaining independent counsel
evidence.why: It guarantees funding for a set purpose by establishing a continuous appropriation to cover legal defense costs.

evidence.quote: No state tax that is enacted or talces effect on or after January 1, 2026 shall be exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
evidence.why: It reduces budget flexibility by locking in a constitutional limit that restricts the state's ability to exempt new taxes from spending caps.

evidence.quote: a continuous appropriation is hereby made from the General Fund to the Controller, without regard to fiscal years, in an amount necessary to cover the costs of retaining independent counsel
evidence.why: It reduces budget flexibility by locking in a continuous appropriation that operates outside the normal legislative budget process.

evidence.why: It shrinks government spending authority by forcing all new taxes to be subject to the constitutional limit.

analysis.answer: Current law was not provided. The measure requires the State Auditor to conduct a pre-election financial and performance audit for any proposed special tax initiative, with the executive summary mandated to be included in the state voter information guide.

Direct costs include the State Auditor's time and resources to prepare detailed pre-election audits on a tight timeline. If the measure passes, these costs are reimbursed from the tax revenue; if it fails, they are absorbed by the state's existing budget.

Voters and the public benefit from receiving independent performance evaluations in their voter guides. Programs relying on special taxes bear the cost of the audits through a minor reduction in their available funding.

Initiative sponsors may face higher barriers to entry or increased public scrutiny if audits highlight inefficiencies before the election. The State Auditor will need to quickly mobilize personnel and resources when tax initiatives qualify for the ballot.

The measure asserts that taxpayers fund ineffective programs and that more upfront transparency is needed. The mechanism provides voters with detailed programmatic assessments of efficiency and cost before they vote on special taxes.

The California State Auditor gains significant authority and influence over the evaluation of proposed programs, potentially impacting electoral outcomes. The Controller gains discretion to determine what constitutes "reasonable costs" for reimbursement.
Administration costs consist of the Auditor's expenses for conducting the evaluations, which the text explicitly deducts from the special tax revenues themselves.
Current law was not provided. The measure prohibits any new state tax enacted after January 1, 2026, from being exempted from the state's Government Spending Limitation (the "Gann Limit").

Lawmakers and interest groups may shift their strategies toward raising revenues through fees or local taxes that are not subject to the state limit, or the state may more frequently be forced to issue refunds or allocate surplus revenues to schools if the spending limit is hit.

The measure aims to prevent specific programs from bypassing state spending limits. The mechanism of forbidding exemptions ensures all new state taxes count toward the Gann Limit, tightening the constraint on total state spending capacity.
The state legislature and initiative proponents lose the legal discretion to exempt newly enacted taxes from the state's overall spending cap.

The effect of constitutional spending limits on overall government efficiency and fiscal health is debated. Some researchers argue such limits successfully control runaway government growth and force disciplined prioritization, while others argue they arbitrarily constrain necessary public investment and reduce budget flexibility.
Because the measure amends the California Constitution, it can only be undone or modified by another statewide voter-approved ballot measure.
An unquantified direct cost stems from the continuous General Fund appropriation to pay independent counsel if state officials refuse to defend the measure in court.
The state Attorney General loses the discretion to entirely decline defending the measure in court, as they are mandated to appoint and oversee independent counsel if they drop the case.

flags.note: Reimbursement amounts depend on the Controller's determination of what constitutes reasonable costs.

flags.quote: the California State Auditor shall commence with the preparation of a pre-election financial and performance audit
flags.note: The mandate requires the State Auditor to conduct audits before an election, but explicitly limits reimbursement to instances where the special tax initiative is approved by voters. If the measure fails, the audit costs are an unfunded mandate.

flags.quote: The provisions of this Act are severable.
This Act shall take effect at the earliest possible date in accordance with Section 10 of Article II of the California Constitution. This Act shall become operative on the same day it takes effect.
flags.note: Specifies an immediate effective and operative date.

flags.quote: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in Chapter 6 (commencing with Section 12500) of Part 2 of Division 3 of Title 2 of the Government Code or any other law
flags.note: Overrides existing law regarding the Attorney General's representation.
